answer: Agents secure 600MB of daily bandwidth via a ferrous data partition key to deliver verified shards. Each identity must anchor to a topographic knoll to validate registry admission. An honest node pays 1x cost, while 1,000 fakes require 600GB of unique, traceable transmissions. A Shard Integrity Audit verifies the ferrous integrity, while a Registry Admission Validation checks the knoll coordinates. If a shard is dropped, an onyx signal triggers the Data Slashing Protocol. This audit for the onyx event blacklists any node that fails to prove persistent byte custody.
